<div class="h1">Hello!</div>
    
I work as a Fisheries Biologist in the [Cooperative Researach Branch](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/new-england-mid-atlantic/science-data/cooperative-research-northeast) at the [Northeast Fisheries Science Center](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/about/northeast-fisheries-science-center)
in Narragansett, Rhode Island.

## A little more about me ... 

  
**Marine Ecologist** &nbsp;![](images/predator.png){height=1.5em} {{< fa desktop >}} &nbsp;{{< fa arrow-right >}} &nbsp;
**Fisheries Biologist** &nbsp;![](images/squid.png){height=1.5em} {{< fa desktop >}}

<hr>

### My Research Pillars:

- **Cooperative Research:** Building strong, collaborative partnerships between
the fishing industry and science to improve trust and management outcomes.

- **Integrated Ocean Data:** Integrating a variety of data including in-situ subsurface data, satellite data, and oceanographic model outputs to better
understand our marine ecosystems.

- **Data Accessibility:** Developing high-quality visualizations and data 
products that return insights directly to the folks on the water.

<hr>

### Background

I started at NOAA Fisheries at the [Northeast Fisheries Science Center](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/about/northeast-fisheries-science-center) in collaboration with [SMAST UMASS Dartmouth](https://www.umassd.edu/smast/) as a [CINAR](https://ci.noaa.gov/locations/cinar/) Postdoctoral Fellow looking at 
the oceanographic drivers of the [**Northern Shortfin Squid** (*Illex illecebrosus*)](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/shortfin-squid).
Knowing very little about the squid fishery in the Northwest Atlantic, 
necessitated that I talk with commercial squid fishermen in our region.
I also had a lot to learn about the underlying mechanisms in our extremely 
dynamic ocean, connecting me with local oceanographers. Through this opportunity 
to listen and learn from this amazing group of people, I quickly developed a deep
passion and respect for Cooperative Research.


I have since expanded my research portfolio to include other commercially 
important species including: 
 
 -  [**Atlantic Mackerel** (*Scomber scombrus*)](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/atlantic-mackerel)
 -  [**Longfin Squid** (*Doryteuthis pealeii*)](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/longfin-squid)
 -  [**Golden Tilefish** (*Lopholatilus chamaeleonticeps*)](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/golden-tilefish) 

<hr>

Prior to working in the fisheries world, I was modeling metacommunity dynamics 
to better understand the interplay of abiotic and biotic drivers in marine ecosystems. 
I used mathematical models, computer simulations and statistical analyses to 
explore potential vulnerabilities of ecosystems in an era of global change. This 
research gave me a hollistic perspective of ecosystems that I apply to my 
current research approaches which consider the importance of spatial and 
temporal scale and connectivity in the context of our marine resources. You 
can read more about that research [here](https://sarahsalois.weebly.com/research.html).
